object.title: Levit–Mandrescu conjecture on independence-equivalent well-covered trees
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $T$ be a well-covered tree, and let $I(G,x)$ denote the independence polynomial of $G$. **Levit–Mandrescu conjecture.** If

$$
I(T,x)=I(G,x),
$$

then $G$ is a well-covered tree. The conjecture concerns whether independence-polynomial equivalence with a well-covered tree forces the other graph to share that structure; the paper later gives an infinite family of counterexamples, so the conjecture is refuted.
object.source_name: Iain Beaton and Ben Cameron, “On the largest real root of the independence polynomial of a unicyclic graph”, arXiv:2006.05511 (2022).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2002–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1309.7673](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.7673), [arXiv:1008.2605](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2605), [arXiv:math/0211036](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211036).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.05511

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2020); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Klein-bottle prism conjecture for hexagonal tessellations
object.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a prism of a hexagonal tessellation of the Klein bottle, and suppose its cutout contains an $m\times n$ array of tiles, with $m$ and $n$ even. Assume that both types of colorings of the hexagonal prism described in the surrounding discussion occur. **Klein-bottle prism conjecture.** The prism is egc, that is, it admits an edge-girth coloring.

This conjecture gives a sufficient parity condition for edge-girth colorability of these Klein-bottle prisms and requires the presence of both local coloring types. The source reports computational evidence in support, but no proof or resolution.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.06956

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

object.title: The planar bichromatic graph algebraic-connectivity conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar bichromatic graph, meaning a planar graph whose vertices can be coloured with two colours so that adjacent vertices have different colours. Let $a(G)$ denote its algebraic connectivity. **Bichromatic planar algebraic-connectivity conjecture.**

$$
a(G)\leq 2.
$$

The preceding discussion gives the weaker bound $a(G)\leq 3$; this conjecture proposes that the bound can be improved to two.

object.title: The divided-differential-operator dimension conjecture for Vandermonde determinants
object.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a prime with $p^2\geq n$, and let $k$ be any field of characteristic $p$. Let $\triangle_n$ be the Vandermonde determinant, let $\mathbb D_n^k$ be the algebra of divided differential operators in $n$ variables, and let

$$
\operatorname{Diff}_n(\triangle_n):=\mathbb C[\partial_{X_1},\dots,\partial_{X_n}]\cdot\triangle_n.
$$

**Divided-differential-operator dimension conjecture.** One has

$$
\dim_k\mathbb D_n^k(\triangle_n)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Diff}_n(\triangle_n).
$$

The paper motivates this as a characteristic-$p$ analogue of the classical Vandermonde dimension result and notes the restriction $p^2\geq n$. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.
object.source_name: Shrawan Kumar and Jesper Funch Thomsen, “A conjectural generalization of n! result to arbitrary groups”, arXiv:math/0201205 (2002).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0201205

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2002).

object.title: Salas–Sokal conjecture for planar bipartite graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar bipartite graph, and let $P(G,t)$ be its chromatic polynomial. Let $\tau=(1+\sqrt{5})/2$ be the golden ratio. **Salas–Sokal conjecture.**

$$
P(G,t)>0\quad\text{for }t\in[\tau^2,\infty).
$$

Equivalently, planar bipartite graphs should have no real chromatic roots at or above $\tau^2$. The source notes that Salas and Sokal constructed families with chromatic roots tending to $\tau^2$, giving evidence for sharpness.
object.source_name: Bill Jackson, “Zeros of Chromatic and Flow Polynomials of Graphs”, arXiv:math/0205047 (2002).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0205047

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2002). “Indeed it is an open problem to determine the supremum of the real chromatic roots of plane triangulations.”

object.title: Circuit-partition unimodality conjecture for weakly Eulerian graphs and digraphs
object.statement: Let a weakly Eulerian graph or digraph be given, and for each integer $k$ let the number of its partitions into $k$ circuits be counted. **Circuit-partition unimodality conjecture.** For any weakly Eulerian graph or digraph, the number of partitions into $k$ circuits is unimodal as a function of $k$. The conjecture is motivated by the circuit-counting interpretation of $xq_G(1+x)$ for interlace graphs and would extend the corresponding unimodality assertion beyond the cases directly represented by interlace polynomials.

object.title: The independence-polynomial characterization of well-covered trees
object.statement:
Let $T$ be a well-covered tree and let $G$ be a graph. Suppose their independence polynomials agree:

$$
I(T;x)=I(G;x).
$$

A graph is **well-covered** if all its maximal stable sets have the same cardinality.

**Independence-polynomial characterization conjecture.** If $T$ is a well-covered tree and $I(T;x)=I(G;x)$, then $G$ is well-covered.

The paper motivates this conjecture by examples of claw-free graphs that are both well-covered and have the same independence polynomials as the well-covered trees under investigation. The source provides no resolution status.

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2002).

object.title: Symmetric-function generalization of the Eremenko–Gabrielov conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition with $\ell$ parts and fixed parity for each part. Let $G_\lambda(x/x)$ be the specialized symmetric function defined by substituting $2p_{2i-1}$ for $p_{2i-1}$ and $0$ for $p_{2i}$, and let $Q_\mu(x)$ denote Schur's shifted $Q$-function. **Symmetric-function generalization of the Eremenko–Gabrielov conjecture.** There are integers $c_1,\dots,c_k$ and integer vectors $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k\in\mathbb{Z}^\ell$ such that

$$
(-1)^{r(\lambda)}G_\lambda(x/x)=\sum_{i=1}^k c_i Q_{\frac12(\lambda+\gamma_i)}(x).
$$

This conjecture is intended as a symmetric-function refinement of the Eremenko–Gabrielov conjecture. The source presents the definition as possibly requiring modification and gives no resolution status.

object.title: Characterization of saturated sets containing no even numbers
object.statement:
Let $G$ be the abelian group under discussion, and call a subset **saturated** if it is a maximal avoidable set. The sets described above are those obtained as solution sets of

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\equiv 1\pmod{2},
$$

where each $a_i$ is $0$ or $1$, not all $0$, in the decomposition of $G$ given in the preceding context. **Characterization conjecture.** The sets described above are the only saturated sets containing no even numbers. This would classify all saturated sets avoiding even elements; the source does not provide evidence resolving the assertion.

object.title: Holroyd–Johnson conjecture for intersecting k-separated sets
object.statement:
Let $[n]^{(r)}_k$ denote the collection of $k$-separated $r$-sets in $[n]^{(r)}$: sets $A=\{a_1,\dots,a_r\}$ with $a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_r$ satisfying $a_{i+1}-a_i>k$ for $i=1,\dots,r$, where $a_{r+1}=a_1+n$. Let $n$, $k$, and $r$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
n\geq (k+1)r.
$$

For an intersecting family $\mathcal{A}\subseteq[n]^{(r)}_k$, define the star at $1$ by

$$
\mathcal{A}_1^*=\{A\in[n]^{(r)}_k:1\in A\}.
$$

**Holroyd and Johnson's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{A}\subseteq[n]^{(r)}_k$ is intersecting, then

$$
|\mathcal{A}|\leq|\mathcal{A}_1^*|.
$$

The conjecture asserts an Erdős–Ko–Rado-type bound for intersecting families of $k$-separated sets. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved; the status is therefore recorded as open.
object.source_name: John Talbot, “Intersecting Families of Separated Sets”, arXiv:math/0211314 (2002).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0211314

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2002). “This was answered in the affirmative by Lov\'asz in 1977 .”

object.title: Higher Narayana number formula for local Weyl modules
object.statement:
Let $W_{\mathbb C^d}(\{0\}_{n\omega})$ be the indicated local Weyl module for $sl_2$, and let $W_{\mathbb C^d}(\{0\}_{n\omega})^{n-2i}$ denote its weight space of weight $n-2i$. **Higher Narayana number conjecture.** For $i=0,\dots,n$, one has

$$
\dim W_{\mathbb C^d}(\{0\}_{n\omega})^{n-2i}=\frac{(d+n-1)!\cdots(d+n-i)!}{(n-1)!\cdots(n-i)!}\cdot\frac{2!\cdots(i-1)!}{d!\cdots(d+i-1)!},
$$

and these dimensions equal the dimension of the irreducible representation of $sl_n$ with highest weight $d\omega_i$ for $i=1,\dots,n-1$, while they equal one for $i=0,n$. This proposes a higher-dimensional analogue of the Catalan and Narayana number formulas established earlier in the paper; the source gives no resolution of the proposed formula.
object.source_name: B. Feigin and S. Loktev, “Multi-dimensional Weyl Modules and Symmetric Functions”, arXiv:math/0212001 (2004).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0212001

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2002).

object.title: The central-circuit characterization of maximal irreducible hedrites
object.statement:
Let $i$ be the number of faces of an irreducible $i$-hedrite, and let a **central circuit** be a central circuit of the hedrite. An irreducible $i$-hedrite is **maximal irreducible** when it cannot be extended while remaining irreducible. **Central-circuit characterization.** An irreducible $i$-hedrite is maximal irreducible if and only if it has $i-2$ central circuits.

The surrounding discussion gives examples of irreducible $i$-hedrites with $i-2$ central circuits for the relevant values of $i$, and notes that these examples are pure. The parser supplies no evidence resolving the stated characterization, so its status remains open.

object.title: Curvature-graph conjecture for tight graphs of type $3_n$
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a tight graph of type $3_n$, and let its graph of curvatures be the $4$-vertex graph associated with the four triangular faces of $G$. The three possible graphs of curvatures are the cases displayed in Proposition/Theorem PossibleGraphCurvature.

**Curvature-graph conjecture.** The graph of curvatures of any tight graph of type $3_n$ is the graph in the first of those three cases.

This conjecture concerns the structure of tight polyhedral graphs with four triangular faces; the source gives the three possible curvature graphs but does not state a resolution of this tighter classification claim.

object.title: The complete bipartite graph ideal degree conjecture
object.statement:
Let $K_{m,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $m$ and $n$, and let $I_{K_{m,n}}$ be its graph ideal. Here $\min\{m,n\}$ denotes the smaller part size.

**Complete bipartite graph ideal degree conjecture.** The graph ideal for $G=K_{m,n}$ is generated in degree at most

$$
2^{\min\{m,n\}}.
$$

This extends the established result for $K_{2,n}$; the paper notes that the conjecture is supported by the preceding result and remains unproved there.
object.source_name: Mike Develin and Seth Sullivant, “Markov bases of binary graph models”, arXiv:math/0308280 (2003).

object.title: The vertex-transitive graph lower-bound conjecture for loop-erased random walk
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite vertex-transitive graph, and let $b$ and $e$ be two random vertices of $G$. Let $R$ be a random walk starting from $b$ and stopped when it hits $e$.

**Loop-erased random walk lower-bound conjecture.** The expected length of the loop-erasure of $R$ satisfies

$$
\mathbb{E}\#\operatorname{LE}(R)\geq c\sqrt{|G|}.
$$

Here $c$ is an absolute positive constant. The vertex-transitivity assumption excludes highly non-transitive examples such as a tree, where the loop-erased walk follows the unique path and can have length of order $\log N$. The conjecture proposes a universal mean-field lower bound for loop-erased random walks on finite vertex-transitive graphs.
object.source_name: Itai Benjamini and Gady Kozma, “Loop-erased random walk on a torus in dimensions 4 and above”, arXiv:math/0309009 (2003).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2003).

object.title: Finiteness conjecture for simplicial complexes of type {3,4,5}
object.statement: A simplicial complex is **of type $\{3,4,5\}$** if the link of every $(n-2)$-face is one of the cycles $C_3$, $C_4$, or $C_5$. **Finiteness conjecture.** In every fixed dimension $n$, there are only finitely many simplicial complexes of type $\{3,4,5\}$. This asserts a finiteness phenomenon for simplicial complexes whose codimension-two links have bounded cycle lengths; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

object.title: The Duval–Reiner conjecture for family-pair Laplacian spectra
object.statement:
Let $(\mathcal K,\mathcal K')$ be a family pair, with relative Laplacian spectrum $\mathbf{s}(\mathcal K,\mathcal K')$ and transposed relative generalized degree sequence $\mathbf{d}(\mathcal K,\mathcal K')^T$. **Family-pair majorization conjecture.**

$$
\mathbf{s}(\mathcal K,\mathcal K')\trianglelefteq\mathbf{d}(\mathcal K,\mathcal K')^T.
$$

This extends the Grone–Merris and Duval–Reiner majorization conjectures from families to family pairs. The text says it is based on only a few examples and does not state a resolution.

object.title: Non-crossing families and labeling sets of plabic diagrams
object.statement: Let $[1\dots n]$ be labeled cyclically, and let a **non-crossing** family be a family of pairwise non-crossing $k$-subsets, where non-crossing means that no chord with endpoints in $I-J$ crosses a chord with endpoints in $J-I$ for two $k$-subsets $I$ and $J$. Let ${\bf D}$ be a $\pi_{k,n}$-diagram, and call the associated $k$-subsets its labeling sets. **Non-crossing families conjecture.** Every maximal family of non-crossing $k$-subsets is a collection of labeling sets for some $\pi_{k,n}$-diagram ${\bf D}$. In particular, every maximal family consists of $k(n-k)+1$ subsets. The preceding corollary establishes the converse inclusion for labeling sets of $\pi_{k,n}$-diagrams. The conjecture asserts that all maximal non-crossing families arise in this way; the source gives no resolution.

object.title: The quadratic-generation conjecture for matroid toric ideals
object.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid and let $I_M$ be its toric ideal. A **quadratic binomial** in $I_M$ is a binomial homogeneous of degree two in the base variables. **The quadratic-generation conjecture.** For any matroid $M$, the toric ideal $I_M$ is generated by quadratic binomials. The source separates this assertion from the stronger symmetric-exchange generation claim; it states that this conjecture and the companion exchange-generation conjecture are both still open and together imply White's conjecture.

object.title: The quadratic symmetric-exchange generation conjecture for matroid toric ideals
object.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid, with toric ideal $I_M$. For bases $B_1,B_2,D_1,D_2$, call $y_{B_1}y_{B_2}-y_{D_1}y_{D_2}$ a **double-swap binomial** when the pair $D_1,D_2$ is obtained from $B_1,B_2$ by a double swap. **The quadratic symmetric-exchange generation conjecture.** For any matroid $M$, the quadratic binomials of $I_M$ are in the ideal generated by the double-swap binomials $y_{B_1}y_{B_2}-y_{D_1}y_{D_2}$. The source identifies this as the second of two open conjectures that together imply White's conjecture.
